source: absmartly/cross-sdk-tests test_scenarios_complete.json @ ada8952293a8d4ebf81f8de038f4e7a406d98870 (main; scenarios 203-227, 230-253, 300-332 and 400-425). Expected values were recorded from the JavaScript reference SDK.

scenarios.name: 203 - Holdouts - Held-Out Unit Suppresses Covered Experiment
scenarios.description: A unit landing in a holdout's variant 0 gets control values for the experiment it covers (no exposure of its own) and exactly one ordinary exposure for the holdout itself.

scenarios.name: 204 - Holdouts - Not-Held-Out Unit Assigns Normally And Exposes Holdout
scenarios.description: A unit outside the holdout's suppressed arm assigns to the covered experiment exactly as it would without holdouts, plus one ordinary exposure for the holdout carrying its nonzero (not-held-out) variant.

scenarios.name: 205 - Holdouts - Union Of Two Holdouts Suppresses Via Higher-Id Holdout
scenarios.description: An experiment covered by two holdouts is suppressed if the unit is held out by EITHER one (union semantics). Pinned so the low-id holdout does NOT hold the unit out and the high-id holdout does, ruling out an implementation that only ever consults holdouts[0]. Both holdouts still emit their own independent exposure.

scenarios.name: 206 - Holdouts - Coverage Is Opt-In Per Experiment
scenarios.description: Holdout coverage never leaks to a sibling experiment lacking holdoutIds, even when that sibling shares the same unit and context as an experiment the same holdout suppresses.

scenarios.name: 207 - Holdouts - Dangling Holdout Id Ignored, Valid Coverage Still Applies
scenarios.description: A holdoutIds entry with no matching holdouts[] element is silently ignored - wire inconsistency tolerance, not an error - while a second, valid id in the same list still applies normally.

scenarios.name: 208 - Holdouts - Suppresses Full-On Experiment Regardless Of Full-On Variant
scenarios.description: A holdout suppresses a full-on experiment (fullOnVariant != 0) exactly as it does a traffic-eligible one - explicit holdoutIds coverage, not full-on status, decides suppression.

scenarios.name: 209 - Holdouts - Old-Payload Tolerance For Uncovered Experiment
scenarios.description: INERTNESS BASELINE (must pass on every SDK, holdout-aware or not): holdouts[] is present in the payload but the experiment under test declares no holdoutIds, so behavior is identical whether or not the SDK understands the holdouts wire format at all. Contrasts with the other Holdouts scenarios in this group, which fail on any SDK that has not implemented holdout resolution.

scenarios.name: 210 - Holdout - Override Takes Precedence Over Holdout
scenarios.description: An explicit override wins over holdout membership for the experiment's own assignment; the override path still evaluates coverage, so the holdout's own exposure fires alongside it

scenarios.name: 211 - Holdout - Holdout Takes Precedence Over Custom Assignment
scenarios.description: Holdout membership forces control and suppresses the experiment's own exposure even with a custom assignment on file; only the holdout's own exposure fires

scenarios.name: 212 - Holdout - Independent Holdouts Across Experiments
scenarios.description: Same unit is held out for one experiment's holdout but not another's, using independent seeds; the held-out experiment fires no exposure of its own while the non-held-out one does

scenarios.name: 213 - Holdout - Consistent Membership Across Shared Holdout
scenarios.description: Same unit and same shared holdout definition produce consistent holdout membership across different experiments; the shared holdout's own exposure fires once on first evaluation and neither covered experiment fires its own exposure

scenarios.name: 214 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 0 Holds Out Full-On And Non-Full-On (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
scenarios.description: A 3-arm holdout's variant 0 forces control for every covered experiment, full-on or not, identically to a 2-arm holdout's variant 0; the holdout's own exposure fires once at variant 0 and neither covered experiment emits its own exposure.

scenarios.name: 215 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 1 Holds Out Non-Full-On, Assigns Full-On Normally (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
scenarios.description: A 3-arm holdout's variant 1 forces control only for a covered experiment with fullOnVariant==0; a covered full-on experiment (fullOnVariant!=0) takes its normal assignment path and is assigned its own fullOnVariant with fullOn=true, not suppressed.

scenarios.name: 216 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 2 Evaluates Both Experiments Normally (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
scenarios.description: A 3-arm holdout's variant 2 (normal traffic) evaluates every covered experiment exactly as if uncovered, full-on or not; the holdout's own exposure fires once at variant 2.

scenarios.name: 217 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 1 Defers To Normal Path For Audience Mismatch (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
scenarios.description: A full-on experiment covered by a 3-arm holdout's variant 1 is not short-circuited to its fullOnVariant: audienceStrict is evaluated first, so an audience mismatch still forces control (not suppression) with assigned=false and audienceMismatch=true; the experiment's own exposure fires because it was evaluated and rejected by audience, not held out.

scenarios.name: 218 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Variant 2 Audience Mismatch Matches Variant 1 Verdict (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
scenarios.description: The same full-on/audience-mismatch experiment, covered instead by the 3-arm holdout's variant 2 (normal traffic), yields the identical verdict as scenario 217's variant 1: control, assigned=false, audienceMismatch=true. This pins that arm 1 defers to the normal assignment path instead of short-circuiting to the full-on variant.

scenarios.name: 219 - Holdout Arms - Union Two-Arm Holds Out While Applicable Three-Arm Does Not (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
scenarios.description: A covered experiment is suppressed if EITHER applicable holdout holds it out, even when a 3-arm holdout's own arm (variant 2, normal traffic) would not have held it out on its own; both holdouts still emit their own independent exposure with their own variant. A second experiment covered only by the non-suppressing 3-arm holdout takes its normal assignment path and emits its own exposure, proving that holdout 22's arm is not itself suppressing.

scenarios.name: 220 - Holdout Arms - Union Three-Arm Variant 1 Holds Out While Applicable Two-Arm Does Not (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
scenarios.description: Union, the other direction: a 3-arm holdout's variant 1 holds a non-full-on covered experiment out even when an applicable 2-arm holdout alone would not have; both holdouts still emit their own independent exposure with their own variant. A second experiment covered only by the non-suppressing 2-arm holdout takes its normal assignment path and emits its own exposure, proving that holdout 11's arm is not itself suppressing.

scenarios.name: 221 - Holdouts - Late Unit Publishes Previously Unavailable Holdout Exposure
scenarios.description: A covered full-on experiment can resolve before its unit type is installed; after setUnit supplies that unit, resolving it again publishes the holdout exposure that was unavailable during the first evaluation.

scenarios.name: 222 - Holdout Arms - Three-Arm Arity Derived From Split Without holdoutType (uid e791e240fcd3df7d238cfc285f475e8152fcc0ec)
scenarios.description: Identical to the three-arm variant 0 scenario, but the holdout definition omits the holdoutType field entirely. An SDK must derive the holdout's arm count from its split length alone, so suppression of both the full-on and non-full-on covered experiments is unchanged. Pins that holdoutType is not required on the wire.

scenarios.name: 223 - Holdouts - Exposure State Survives Publish
scenarios.description: Holdout and experiment exposures are once per context, not once per publish: after the queue is flushed, calling treatment again on the same experiment, or on another experiment covered by the same holdout, queues nothing. Covers both a held-out holdout (suppressed experiments) and a not-held-out one (normal experiment exposure plus holdout exposure).

scenarios.name: 224 - Holdouts - Refresh Keeps Exposure Unless Holdout Iteration Changes
scenarios.description: A refresh with identical data keeps the holdout's exposure state, so neither the covered experiment nor a sibling covered by the same holdout re-exposes it. A refresh that bumps the holdout's iteration starts a new epoch: the next covered treatment publishes one new holdout exposure, and the sibling then shares it.

scenarios.name: 225 - Holdouts - Refresh Adding Or Removing Coverage Re-Resolves Experiment
scenarios.description: An experiment's holdout set is part of its assignment epoch. A refresh that adds a held-out holdout to holdoutIds re-resolves an already-exposed experiment: it is suppressed to control and the holdout exposure fires. A refresh that removes the coverage again restores its normal assignment with a fresh experiment exposure.

scenarios.name: 226 - Holdouts - Variable Value Of Suppressed Experiment Returns Control
scenarios.description: For a held-out unit, variableValue on a covered experiment returns the control variant's value (not the caller's default and not the unit's would-be treatment value), peekVariableValue does the same without queuing anything, and the first variableValue fires only the holdout's exposure. A later treatment call on the same experiment queues nothing.

scenarios.name: 227 - Holdouts - Holdout Resolves Per Covered Experiment Unit Type
scenarios.description: A holdout is evaluated with the covered experiment's unitType, not the holdout's own declared unitType (matching the java-sdk reference implementation). One holdout covering experiments of two unit types therefore yields one exposure per unit type, each carrying that unit; a second experiment of an already-exposed unit type would not re-expose it.

scenarios.name: 230 - Custom Assignment Rules - Matching Assign Rule Wins And Flags ruleOverride
scenarios.description: An assign rule whose condition matches sets the variant; the exposure is flagged ruleOverride:true with assigned:false (the backend excludes it from analysis), not custom. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 231 - Custom Assignment Rules - Non-Matching Assign Rule Falls Through To Normal Assignment
scenarios.description: An assign rule whose condition does not match is skipped and the unit takes its ordinary assignment (variant 1 here, assigned:true, ruleOverride:false). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 232 - Custom Assignment Rules - Out-Of-Range Rule Variant Is Ignored And Later Rules Are Not Tried
scenarios.description: The first matching rule's variant (5) is out of range for a two-variant experiment, so normal assignment applies and the second rule (variant 0) is NOT tried: the unit gets its ordinary assignment (variant 1), not variant 0. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 233 - Custom Assignment Rules - Split Rule Randomizes Over Its Own Percentages And Flags ruleOverride
scenarios.description: A split rule with percentages 0/100 sends every unit to variant 1 over the rule's own percentages; the exposure is flagged ruleOverride:true, assigned:false. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 234 - Custom Assignment Rules - Environment-Scoped Rule Does Not Match A Different Environment
scenarios.description: A rule scoped to environment 'production' does not match the reference context's environment, so it is skipped and the unit takes its ordinary assignment (variant 1). 'production' is used because it matches no SDK wrapper's environment name. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 235 - Custom Assignment Rules - Override Beats A Matching Rule
scenarios.description: setOverride wins over every rule: with a rule that would assign variant 1, an override to variant 2 gives variant 2 with overridden:true (ruleOverride:false, assigned:false). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 236 - Custom Assignment Rules - Rule Takes Precedence Over A Strict Audience Mismatch
scenarios.description: A matching rule is evaluated before audience targeting: even though the strict audience (tier == gold) does not match, the rule assigns variant 1 with ruleOverride:true and audienceMismatch:false (audience is not evaluated for a rule win). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 237 - Custom Assignment Rules - Rule Takes Precedence Over A Custom Assignment
scenarios.description: A matching rule wins over a custom assignment: customAssignment(2) is set, but the rule assigns variant 1 with ruleOverride:true (custom:false). The custom assignment only shows when no rule matches. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 238 - Custom Assignment Rules - Variable Value Is Served Through A Rule Win
scenarios.description: variableValue resolves through a rule-won assignment (assigned:false but ruleOverride): the rule assigns variant 1, so variableValue('color') returns variant 1's 'blue' and queues the rule-flagged exposure. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 239 - Custom Assignment Rules - Rule Variant Of A Removed Experiment Is Rebuilt, Not Served Stale
scenarios.description: javascript-sdk#67 edge case: a rule assigns variant 1 (ruleOverride:true). After a refresh whose data no longer contains the experiment, the cached rule variant is dropped and the experiment is rebuilt to variant 0 (assigned:false, ruleOverride:false) with a fresh exposure, instead of serving the stale rule variant. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 240 - Semver Operators - semver_gte Matches (1.5.0 vs 1.2.0)
scenarios.description: Strict audience uses semver_gte; with app_version='1.5.0' the filter matches (1.5.0 >= 1.2.0 is true), so the unit gets variant 1 (assigned). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 241 - Semver Operators - semver_gte Does Not Match (1.1.0 vs 1.2.0)
scenarios.description: Strict audience uses semver_gte; with app_version='1.1.0' the filter does not match (1.1.0 >= 1.2.0 is false), so the unit gets variant 0 with audienceMismatch:true. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 242 - Semver Operators - semver_eq Matches (v1.2 vs 1.2.0+build)
scenarios.description: Strict audience uses semver_eq; with app_version='v1.2' the filter matches (v1.2 == 1.2.0+build: leading v and +build metadata are ignored, missing patch is 0), so the unit gets variant 1 (assigned). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 243 - Semver Operators - semver_gt Matches (1.10.0 vs 1.9.0)
scenarios.description: Strict audience uses semver_gt; with app_version='1.10.0' the filter matches (1.10.0 > 1.9.0: numeric identifiers compare numerically, not lexicographically), so the unit gets variant 1 (assigned). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 244 - Semver Operators - semver_lt Matches (1.0.0-beta vs 1.0.0)
scenarios.description: Strict audience uses semver_lt; with app_version='1.0.0-beta' the filter matches (1.0.0-beta < 1.0.0: a pre-release ranks below its release), so the unit gets variant 1 (assigned). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 245 - Semver Operators - semver_lte Matches (2.0.0 vs 2.0.0)
scenarios.description: Strict audience uses semver_lte; with app_version='2.0.0' the filter matches (2.0.0 <= 2.0.0 is true), so the unit gets variant 1 (assigned). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 246 - Audience Re-Evaluation - Setting An Attribute That Satisfies A Strict Audience Reassigns And Re-Exposes
scenarios.description: A strict audience (tier == gold) is unmatched at first, so treatment is variant 0 with audienceMismatch:true. Setting tier=gold re-evaluates the audience on the next treatment: the unit now matches, is assigned variant 1, and a fresh exposure is queued (pending grows). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 247 - Audience Re-Evaluation - Setting An Attribute That Breaks A Strict Audience Reassigns To Control
scenarios.description: The mirror case: tier=gold matches first (variant 1, assigned). Setting tier=silver re-evaluates the audience on the next treatment: the unit no longer matches, is reassigned variant 0 with audienceMismatch:true, and a fresh exposure is queued. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 248 - System Attributes - Strict Audience On The Configured Environment Matches And Serves The Variant
scenarios.description: §4.1 + variable read: a strict audience (environment == the configured environment name) matches because the SDK always injects the client's environment into the evaluation map, so the unit is assigned variant 1 with audienceMismatch:false, and variableValue('color') reads the matched variant 1's 'blue' through the same assignment. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 249 - System Attributes - Strict Audience On The Configured Application Matches
scenarios.description: §4.1 (application): a strict audience (application == the configured application name) matches because the SDK always injects the client's application into the evaluation map, so the unit is assigned variant 1 with audienceMismatch:false. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 250 - System Attributes - Strict Audience On A Different Environment Does Not Match
scenarios.description: §4.3: a strict audience (environment == 'other-env') does not match the configured environment, so the unit gets variant 0 with audienceMismatch:true. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 251 - System Attributes - A User-Set Environment Overrides The Configured One And Invalidates The Cache
scenarios.description: §4.4: the configured environment matches at first (peek -> variant 1). Setting environment='other-env' as a user attribute overlays the system value and wins: the cached assignment is invalidated and the next treatment reassigns the unit to variant 0 with audienceMismatch:true and a fresh exposure. The strict audience names the configured environment, so only a user value that overrides it can flip the result. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 252 - System Attributes - A User-Set Environment Satisfies An Audience The Configured One Did Not
scenarios.description: §4.4 (mirror): the configured environment does not match the strict audience (environment == 'other-env'), so the unit starts at variant 0 with audienceMismatch:true. Setting environment='other-env' as a user attribute overlays the system value, matches the audience, and reassigns the unit to variant 1 with a fresh exposure. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 253 - System Attributes - No Environment Configured Means A Strict Environment Audience Does Not Match
scenarios.description: §4.6: with the application configured but NO environment, the SDK leaves environment out of the evaluation map entirely, so a strict audience on environment does not match and the unit gets variant 0 with audienceMismatch:true (no crash). An application audience still matches, confirming the application was injected while the environment was left absent. A third, absence-sensitive audience (environment IS present, via not/null) must ALSO miss: a wrapper that substitutes a placeholder environment instead of leaving it absent would wrongly match this one even though it also fails the equality check against the real name. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 300 - Assignment Rules - Split Rule Hashes Each Unit With The Experiment Seed
scenarios.description: A 20/30/50 split rule assigns three units (one per unit type) to variants 0, 1 and 2. The units are pinned so that each variant differs from what the traffic seed, swapped seeds, zero seeds or the experiment's own split would give: only hashing the unit with the experiment's seedHi/seedLo over the rule's percentages passes. Each exposure is ruleOverride:true, assigned:false, eligible:true. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 301 - Assignment Rules - Environment Scoping Matches Listed, Skips Unlisted, Empty List Matches Everywhere
scenarios.description: With the client environment 'parity-env': a rule listing it matches (variant 0, ruleOverride), a rule listing only other environments is skipped (normal assignment, variant 1), and a rule with an empty environments list matches every environment. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 302 - Assignment Rules - No Environment Configured Skips Environment-Scoped Rules Only
scenarios.description: With no client environment, a rule scoped to environments is skipped (normal assignment), while a rule with an empty environments list and a rule with no environments key still match. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 303 - Assignment Rules - First Matching Rule Wins
scenarios.description: Two rules both match; the first one's variant (2) wins over the second's (1). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 304 - Assignment Rules - False Condition Falls Through To The Next Rule
scenarios.description: The first rule's condition is false (country is CA), so evaluation continues and the second rule assigns variant 0 with ruleOverride:true. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 305 - Assignment Rules - Rule Wins Over Holdout Suppression
scenarios.description: Both experiments are covered by a holdout whose split holds every unit out. The one with a matching rule still serves the rule variant (1) with a ruleOverride exposure; the one without a rule is suppressed to variant 0. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 306 - Assignment Rules - Rule Wins Over Traffic Split And Full-On
scenarios.description: A unit outside the traffic split (trafficSplit [1, 0]) still gets the rule variant 1 (eligible:true, ruleOverride); without the rule it gets 0 with eligible:false. A rule assigning variant 1 also beats fullOnVariant 2 (fullOn:false). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 307 - Assignment Rules - Rule Beating A Different Custom Assignment Exposes Once
scenarios.description: javascript-sdk#66 fix: a rule assigns variant 1 although customAssignment(2) is set. Repeated treatment() and variableValue() calls keep returning the rule variant and queue exactly one exposure, instead of treating the custom mismatch as a stale assignment and re-exposing on every call. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 308 - Assignment Rules - Split Rule Without Its Unit Gives Variant 0, Then Re-Resolves Once The Unit Is Set
scenarios.description: The split rule matches but its unit type (session_id) is not set: the experiment's no-unit result applies (variant 0, not full-on). The assignment is not exposed (peek), so setting the unit re-resolves it through the split (variant 1) and the first treatment exposes that with ruleOverride:true. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 309 - Assignment Rules - Split Rule Exposed Without Its Unit Stays Pinned After The Unit Is Set
scenarios.description: The split rule matches without its unit and treatment() exposes the no-unit result (variant 0). Setting the unit and then an attribute (which re-evaluates the assignment) does not move the user: treatment still returns 0 and no second exposure is queued. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 310 - Assignment Rules - Split Rule Without Its Unit On A Full-On Experiment Gives The Full-On Variant
scenarios.description: On a full-on experiment (fullOnVariant 2) a split rule matching without its unit gives the full-on variant; once the unit is set (not yet exposed) it re-resolves through the split. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 311 - Assignment Rules - Malformed Split Rules Are Skipped For The Next Rule
scenarios.description: A split rule whose percentages are a number, non-numeric, negative, sum to 90, or are missing is skipped, and the next rule (assign variant 0) wins with ruleOverride:true. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 312 - Assignment Rules - Wrong-Count Split And Negative Assign Variant Stop Rule Evaluation
scenarios.description: A split with three values on a two-variant experiment, and an assign rule with variant -1, each stop rule evaluation: the later assign-0 rule is NOT tried and the unit gets its normal assignment (variant 1, assigned:true, ruleOverride:false). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 313 - Assignment Rules - Split Percentages Must Sum To 100 Within 0.01
scenarios.description: '50/50.014' (gap 0.014, rounded to 0.01) is accepted and splits the unit to variant 1; '50/50.015' (gap rounds to 0.02) is skipped and the next rule assigns variant 0 (the same unit would split to variant 1, so accepting it is visible). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 314 - Assignment Rules - Rule Condition Uses A Semver Operator
scenarios.description: A rule condition semver_gte(app_version, 2.0.0) matches 2.1.0 (variant 0 via the rule) and stops matching when app_version is set to 1.9.9 (normal assignment, variant 1). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 315 - Semver Comparison - semver_eq Normalizes Prefix, Missing Parts And Build Metadata
scenarios.description: semver_eq ignores a leading v, treats missing parts as 0, ignores build metadata, and distinguishes a different patch and a pre-release from its release. Cases, in order: semver_eq("v1.2.3", "1.2.3"); semver_eq("1.2", "1.2.0"); semver_eq("1.0.0+a", "1.0.0+b"); semver_eq("1.2.3", "1.2.4"); semver_eq("1.0.0-rc.1", "1.0.0"). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 316 - Semver Comparison - semver_gt And semver_gte Compare Numerically
scenarios.description: semver_gt/semver_gte compare numeric identifiers numerically (1.10.0 > 1.9.9), rank a release above its pre-release, and treat build metadata as equal. Cases, in order: semver_gt("1.10.0", "1.9.9"); semver_gt("2.0.0", "2.0.0-rc.1"); semver_gt("1.0.0", "1.0.0"); semver_gt("1.0.0+b", "1.0.0+a"); semver_gte("1.0.0", "1.0.0"); semver_gte("0.9.10", "0.10.0"); semver_gte("1.0.0+build.9", "1.0.0"). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 317 - Semver Comparison - semver_lt And semver_lte Compare Numerically
scenarios.description: semver_lt/semver_lte mirror gt/gte, including the pre-release and equal boundaries. Cases, in order: semver_lt("1.9.9", "1.10.0"); semver_lt("1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0"); semver_lt("1.0.0", "1.0.0"); semver_lte("1.0.0", "1.0.0"); semver_lte("1.0.1", "1.0.0"); semver_lte("1.0.0-rc.1", "1.0.0-rc.1"). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 318 - Semver Comparison - Pre-Release Precedence Follows The semver.org Chain
scenarios.description: Each step of 1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0-alpha.1 < 1.0.0-alpha.beta < 1.0.0-beta < 1.0.0-beta.2 < 1.0.0-beta.11 < 1.0.0-rc.1 < 1.0.0 holds under semver_lt, and the reverse does not (numeric identifiers rank below alphanumeric ones, a longer identifier list ranks above its prefix, and numeric identifiers compare numerically). Cases, in order: semver_lt("1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0-alpha.1"); semver_lt("1.0.0-alpha.1", "1.0.0-alpha.beta"); semver_lt("1.0.0-alpha.beta", "1.0.0-beta"); semver_lt("1.0.0-beta", "1.0.0-beta.2"); semver_lt("1.0.0-beta.2", "1.0.0-beta.11"); semver_lt("1.0.0-beta.11", "1.0.0-rc.1"); semver_lt("1.0.0-rc.1", "1.0.0"); semver_lt("1.0.0-beta.11", "1.0.0-beta.2"); semver_lt("1.0.0-alpha.beta", "1.0.0-alpha.1"). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 319 - Semver Comparison - Invalid And Missing Versions Evaluate Like The Reference
scenarios.description: An empty version, a bare 'v', a bare '+build', an unset attribute and an empty right-hand side make the comparison null, so a strict audience does not match. Numbers are compared as their string form (2 > 1.9.9), and a non-numeric core is compared as an alphanumeric identifier, which ranks above any numeric one (so 'abc' > 1.0.0 and 'abc' < 1.0.0 is false), exactly as the JS reference does. Cases, in order: semver_eq("", "1.0.0"); semver_eq("v", "1.0.0"); semver_eq("+build", "1.0.0"); semver_gte(null, "1.0.0"); semver_lte("1.0.0", ""); semver_gt(2, "1.9.9"); semver_gt("abc", "1.0.0"); semver_lt("abc", "1.0.0"). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 320 - X-Agent - Context Fetch Sends absmartly-<lang>-sdk/<version>
scenarios.description: The SDK's own GET {endpoint}/context request carries an X-Agent header of the form absmartly-<lang>-sdk/<semver>. The wrapper records the request it served (capturedRequests).

scenarios.name: 321 - X-Agent - Publish Sends absmartly-<lang>-sdk/<version>
scenarios.description: The SDK's own PUT {endpoint}/context publish request carries an X-Agent header of the form absmartly-<lang>-sdk/<semver>. The context is created with publishToEndpoint so the SDK's real publisher sends to the wrapper's mock collector, which records the request.

scenarios.name: 322 - Client Application - An Explicitly Blank Application Is Rejected
scenarios.description: POST /context with client.application "" on an SDK whose client rejects a blank application: the wrapper forwards the value unchanged, so creation fails with the SDK's own validation error as a 400. A wrapper that repairs the blank name into its default application returns a ready context instead and fails.

scenarios.name: 323 - Client Application - An Explicitly Blank Application Is Left Out Of The Evaluation Map
scenarios.description: POST /context with client.application "" on an SDK that accepts a blank application: the SDK leaves application out of the evaluation map, so a strict audience requiring application to be present misses (variant 0, audienceMismatch:true), while the configured environment still matches. A wrapper that repairs the blank name into its default application makes the first audience match and fails. Expectations follow the system-attributes contract (scenario 253's absence check), not the JS reference, which rejects a blank application.

scenarios.name: 324 - Assignment Rules - Rule Conditions Read The Configured Application And Environment
scenarios.description: With client application 'sysattr-app' and environment 'sysattr-env' and no user attributes, a rule conditioned on environment and a rule conditioned on application both match (variant 0, ruleOverride:true); an SDK that evaluates rule conditions on user attributes only gives the normal variant 1. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 325 - Assignment Rules - A User-Set Environment Overrides The Configured One In Rule Conditions
scenarios.description: With client environment 'sysattr-env', the user sets attribute environment 'user-env': a rule conditioned on the configured name no longer matches (normal variant 1, ruleOverride:false) and a rule conditioned on the user value matches (variant 0, ruleOverride:true). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 326 - Assignment Rules - Rule Environment Scope Uses The Configured Environment, Not A User-Set One
scenarios.description: With client environment 'sysattr-env', the user sets attribute environment 'user-env'. A rule scoped to environments ['user-env'] is skipped (normal variant 1, ruleOverride:false) and a rule scoped to the configured environment still matches (variant 0, ruleOverride:true): a user attribute overrides conditions, never the scope. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 327 - Assignment Rules - Split Percentages Parse A Numeric Prefix Like parseFloat
scenarios.description: '0abc/100' parses as 0/100 (parseFloat reads the numeric prefix), so the split rule is valid and assigns variant 1 with ruleOverride:true; a parser that rejects trailing text skips it and the fallback rule assigns variant 0. 'abc/100' has no numeric prefix, so it is invalid (NaN) and the fallback assigns variant 0; a parser that maps garbage to 0 (atof, to_f) accepts it as 0/100 and assigns variant 1. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 328 - Assignment Rules - Unknown Rule Types And Malformed Rule Fields Are Skipped For The Next Rule
scenarios.description: A rule of an unknown type ('pin', carrying a variant), an assign rule with a fractional variant (1.5), and a rule whose environments is a string rather than a list are each skipped, and the next rule (assign variant 0) wins with ruleOverride:true. The string scope names the configured environment, so an SDK that accepted it as a one-item list would match it. A future rule type must never be served as an assign rule. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 329 - Assignment Rules - A Rule Changed Or Removed On Refresh Re-Resolves The Assignment
scenarios.description: Both experiments start with a matching assign-0 rule (variant 0, ruleOverride:true). A refresh changes the first experiment's rule to one whose condition no longer matches and removes the second experiment's rules: each now gets its normal variant 1 with a fresh exposure (ruleOverride:false) instead of the stale rule variant. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 330 - Assignment Rules - Invalid Assignment Rules JSON Stays Isolated To Its Experiment
scenarios.description: An experiment whose assignmentRules is not valid JSON gets its normal assignment (variant 1, ruleOverride:false), and the next experiment's valid assign-0 rule still applies: one bad rules string never fails the context or other experiments. Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 331 - Semver Comparison - Leading Zeros In Numeric Identifiers Are Ignored
scenarios.description: Leading zeros in a numeric identifier are ignored, so 01.0.0 equals 1.0.0. Cases, in order: semver_eq("01.0.0", "1.0.0"). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 332 - Semver Comparison - A Numeric Operand Compares As Its Fixed-Point String
scenarios.description: A numeric attribute is converted like JS toFixed(15) with trailing zeros trimmed, so 1e-7 equals 0.0000001 (not '1E-07'). Cases, in order: semver_eq(1e-07, "0.0000001"). Expected results recorded from @absmartly/javascript-sdk 1.14.0 (javascript-sdk#68).

scenarios.name: 400 - Switchback - Golden Vectors - assignSwitchback - 2 Arms
scenarios.description: Every 2-arm assignSwitchback case (294) of the platform golden vectors, driven through POST /switchback/assign. 64-bit values travel as decimal strings; integer cluster units are sent as their decimal string.

scenarios.name: 401 - Switchback - Golden Vectors - assignSwitchback - 3 Arms
scenarios.description: Every 3-arm assignSwitchback case (294) of the platform golden vectors, driven through POST /switchback/assign. 64-bit values travel as decimal strings; integer cluster units are sent as their decimal string.

scenarios.name: 402 - Switchback - Golden Vectors - assignSwitchback - 10 Arms
scenarios.description: Every 10-arm assignSwitchback case (294) of the platform golden vectors, driven through POST /switchback/assign. 64-bit values travel as decimal strings; integer cluster units are sent as their decimal string.

scenarios.name: 403 - Switchback - Golden Vectors - fisherYatesPermutation - 2 Arms
scenarios.description: Every 2-arm fisherYatesPermutation case (168) of the platform golden vectors, driven through POST /switchback/permutation. The permutation is compared positionally.

scenarios.name: 404 - Switchback - Golden Vectors - fisherYatesPermutation - 3 Arms
scenarios.description: Every 3-arm fisherYatesPermutation case (168) of the platform golden vectors, driven through POST /switchback/permutation. The permutation is compared positionally.

scenarios.name: 405 - Switchback - Golden Vectors - fisherYatesPermutation - 10 Arms
scenarios.description: Every 10-arm fisherYatesPermutation case (168) of the platform golden vectors, driven through POST /switchback/permutation. The permutation is compared positionally.

scenarios.name: 406 - Switchback - Single Source - Raw Attribute Value Is The Cluster Key
scenarios.description: switchbackClusters {store_id: <path>} with one store_id unit. The cluster key is the raw attribute value: variant = assignSwitchback(value, periodIndex, seed, arms) with periodIndex = floorDiv(now - switchbackStartAt, switchbackPeriodMs) (period 0 for the 3- and 10-arm experiments, period 1 for the 2-arm one). Each value is chosen so the draw is nonzero and differs from a hashed key, the uid as key, the hashed uid as key, a Phase 1E bucket and the sticky unit assignment. Each exposure is under the serving unit store_id. exp_sb_eligible_control (3 arms, period 0) is the eligible control: city0='control-8' draws 0, so it serves variant 0 with assigned=true, eligible=true and the exposure is recorded and published; a hashed key, the uid as key, the hashed uid as key, a Phase 1E bucket and the sticky unit assignment all draw nonzero there, and so does a model that maps a 0 draw to 1.

scenarios.name: 407 - Switchback - Declared Order - Lower-Declared Source Serves Whatever The Context Unit Order
scenarios.description: Both units carry the same cluster value (agreement), so both experiments are eligible. The context sets user_id before session_id. exp_sb_order_session_first declares session_id first and must serve and expose under session_id; exp_sb_order_user_first declares user_id first and must serve under user_id. A units-outer iteration (context order) or a last-unit-serves model exposes the wrong unit in at least one of them, whatever order the SDK keeps its units in.

scenarios.name: 408 - Switchback - Agreement - Equal Values From Two Units Serve The Cluster
scenarios.description: session_store and profile/store hold the same value: the units agree and the first declared (session_id) serves with that raw value as the cluster key.

scenarios.name: 409 - Switchback - Disagreement - Different Values Are An Ineligible Control With No Exposure
scenarios.description: session_store='left-1' and profile/store_d='right-1' disagree: variant 0 and no exposure (pending stays 0). Either value alone would draw a nonzero variant, so a first-value-wins or last-value-wins SDK fails, and an SDK that records the ineligible control (eligible=false) fails the exposure check.

scenarios.name: 410 - Switchback - Unit Without A Value Is Skipped - The Next Unit Serves
scenarios.description: session_id is declared first but session_zone is unset; user_id's profile/zone has a value, so user_id serves and the exposure is under user_id.

scenarios.name: 411 - Switchback - Values - Strings And Whole Numbers Only
scenarios.description: A non-empty string is the key as-is and a whole number is keyed by its decimal text: store_number=4000000002 draws assignSwitchback("4000000002", ...), unlike its int32 wrap or double renderings, and agrees with the string "4000000002" from another unit type. 1.5, 3.0, true, an object, an array, "" and null give no value: each such experiment is an ineligible control with no exposure, although its lax text rendering would draw nonzero.

scenarios.name: 412 - Switchback - Attribute Paths - Platform Path Cases And Malformed Paths
scenarios.description: One experiment per case of the platform's attribute-path-cases.json (fixture attributes set as top-level attributes): a supported path that resolves to a value serves that value as the cluster key; a supported path that resolves to nothing ("+0" and "\u0660" are keys, not indices) is an ineligible control with no exposure; an unsupported path (a negative or misplaced index) makes the cluster map unreadable, which takes the legacy path (ineligible control under unitType, no exposure). Added cases: "tags/0" and "m/0/0/city" (index at the tail, two indices in a row), "geo.city", "'geo.city'", "\"geo.city\"" and "dot.city" (any '.' in a segment key is malformed, quoted or not, even though dot/city resolves) and "'geo" (unterminated quote). Where a lax reader would find a value, the seeds make that draw nonzero.

scenarios.name: 413 - Switchback - Allow-List - In, Out, Null And Empty
scenarios.description: switchbackClusterValues filters the cluster key: a value in the list serves; a value outside it is an ineligible control with no exposure (its draw would be nonzero); null and [] both admit every value (the Collector builds its filter only for a non-empty list).

scenarios.name: 414 - Switchback - Schedule - Pre-Anchor And Unservable Schedules Are Silent Controls
scenarios.description: The cluster is eligible (city is set) but the draw cannot run: now is before switchbackStartAt (2100-01-01), the anchor is not hour aligned (anchor+1 ms; never rounded, though the hour-ceiled anchor would draw nonzero), the anchor is absent, the period is 0, or the split has one arm. Each is variant 0 and records no exposure (the SDK's documented pre-anchor choice), and never falls back to sticky unit assignment (the uid's unit draw is nonzero).

scenarios.name: 415 - Switchback - Traffic - Miss On An Eligible Cluster Is Recorded Eligible=False Under The Serving Unit
scenarios.description: trafficSplit 50/50, hashed on the serving unit's uid. Both units agree on the cluster value. In exp_sb_traffic_session_serves session_id (declared first) serves and its uid misses traffic: variant 0 and an exposure under session_id with eligible=false is recorded. In exp_sb_traffic_user_serves user_id serves and its uid is in traffic, so the cluster's draw is served. Each experiment's unitType names the other unit, so hashing traffic on unitType flips both outcomes.

scenarios.name: 416 - Switchback - Precedence - Override, Assignment Rule, Strict Audience, Full-On And Custom Over The Draw
scenarios.description: The cluster's period-0 draw is 1. An override to 2 wins (assigned=false, overridden=true); an assign rule to 2 wins (assigned=false, ruleOverride=true), also before the anchor; a strict audience mismatch (tier silver, audience tier gold) serves 0 with assigned=false and audienceMismatch=true, recorded, as for unit experiments; fullOnVariant=2 wins (fullOn=true), also before the anchor; a custom assignment to 2 is served after traffic (custom=true). Every exposure is under the serving unit store_id. exp_sb_override_no_value has no cluster value (unset_zone is never set) and its override to 2 still applies (overridden=true, under the first declared unit type store_id, not its unitType user_id); exp_sb_full_on_ineligible has fullOnVariant=2 but a value outside switchbackClusterValues, so it is an ineligible control (0, no exposure: full-on is never evaluated for an ineligible cluster); exp_sb_custom_traffic_miss has trafficSplit [0.5, 0.5] that the serving uid misses and a custom assignment to 2: the traffic miss wins (0, recorded eligible=false, custom=false). exp_sb_rule_ineligible has an assign rule to 2 but a value outside switchbackClusterValues, and exp_sb_strict_ineligible has a strict audience the context mismatches but no cluster value (unset_zone): both are ineligible controls (0, no exposure; neither the rule nor the audience is evaluated for an ineligible cluster).

scenarios.name: 417 - Switchback - Holdouts Never Apply To A Switchback
scenarios.description: The switchback is covered by a holdout whose split [1, 0] holds every unit out (variant 0). Holdouts never apply to a switchback: the cluster's draw is served, exactly one exposure (the switchback's own) is recorded and the holdout records none.

scenarios.name: 418 - Switchback - Legacy Path - Missing Or Empty Cluster Map, No Linked Unit, Phase 1E Fields Ignored
scenarios.description: switchbackClusters absent or {} (also when only the abandoned switchbackClusterUnitType/Count/Attribute fields are present) takes the Collector's legacy path: a store_id unit (the declared unitType) gets an ineligible control, variant 0 and no exposure, never sticky unit assignment (the uid's unit draw is nonzero). A cluster map whose only unit type the context lacks does not apply: variant 0, no exposure. An experiment with switchbackClusters {store_id: city} that also carries the Phase 1E fields pointing at user_id/zone is served from city under store_id; reading the legacy fields would draw differently.

scenarios.name: 419 - Switchback - Refresh - A Changed Cluster Map Re-Resolves And Re-Exposes
scenarios.description: city='rcity-0' draws 2. A refresh changes the cluster path to zone ('rzone-4' draws 1): a new epoch, so the next treatment re-resolves and records a new exposure even though the period is unchanged. An unchanged switchback keeps its cached assignment and exposes once.

scenarios.name: 420 - Switchback - Exposure And Publish Payload Carry No New Fields
scenarios.description: A unit experiment on the same unit is exposed and published first as the baseline. The switchback exposure and its publish event must then have exactly the baseline's fields at every depth (sameShapeAs), with every exposure field value pinned, so a switchback-only field such as a period index or cluster key fails the scenario. A second treatment in the same period exposes nothing.

scenarios.name: 421 - Switchback - Inertness - Unit Experiments Unaffected By Switchback Data
scenarios.description: INERTNESS BASELINE (must pass on every SDK, switchback-aware or not): the payload carries a switchback experiment and unit experiments, two of which also carry every R33 switchback wire field (an ordered switchbackClusters over both context units, switchbackClusterValues admitting the city that is set) and the abandoned Phase 1E fields (one with randomizationType "unit", one with it absent). Each unit experiment's treatment, exposure and published exposure equal plain unit assignment in every field; the uid's unit variant is 1 while the city's cluster draw is 0, so serving a unit experiment as a switchback fails. Each exposure and publish event has exactly the fields of the plain unit experiment's at every depth. The switchback experiment is never queried: an SDK without switchback serves it a sticky unit assignment that is documented and SDK-specific.

scenarios.name: 422 - Switchback - Read Once Per Period - A Later setAttribute Does Not Move The Slot
scenarios.description: city='once-a-2' draws 2; city is then set to 'once-b-18', which alone would draw 1. The second treatment in the same period keeps the first variant and records no second exposure (one exposure in total). exp_sb_read_once_ineligible is read while zone is unset (ineligible: 0, no exposure); zone is then set to 'once-z-1' (which would draw 1), and the next treatment in the same period is still 0 with no exposure.

scenarios.name: 423 - Switchback - Peek And Variable Values Resolve The Cluster Draw
scenarios.description: Every arm has a different sb_banner value. The cluster's draw is 2: peekVariableValue and peek return banner-2 / 2 with no exposure; variableValue returns banner-2 and records the one exposure; a later treatment returns the same variant and records nothing.

scenarios.name: 424 - Switchback - Holdout And Assignment Rule - The Rule Wins And The Holdout Is Never Consulted
scenarios.description: One payload: a holdout whose split [1, 0] holds every store_id unit out covers two switchbacks served from the same cluster (period-0 draw 2). exp_sb_holdout_rule also has an assign rule to 1: the rule wins (variant 1, assigned=false, ruleOverride=true), never the holdout's control. exp_sb_holdout_no_rule serves the draw 2 (ruleOverride=false). The holdout never applies to a switchback, so exactly the two switchback exposures are queued and published and the holdout records none: an SDK that evaluates the holdout before the rule serves 0, and one that fires the covering holdout's exposure as for a unit experiment publishes a third exposure.

scenarios.name: 425 - Switchback - Many Sources - Declared Cluster Order Is Kept, Not Sorted
scenarios.description: switchbackClusters has three entries whose JSON key order is the declared order and is neither alphabetical nor reverse alphabetical: exp_sb_many_user_first declares user_id, device_id, store_id and exp_sb_many_store_first declares store_id, user_id, device_id. Every source path holds the same value ('many-3'), so the units agree and the first declared unit serves. Each experiment's trafficSplit [0.5, 0.5] is in for its first declared unit's uid and out for the other two, so the cluster's draw is served under the first declared unit; an SDK that decodes the cluster map into a sorted or other unordered map serves another unit, which misses traffic (variant 0, eligible=false, exposed under the wrong unit).
